hypothesis: An intermediate grid of 384 CTAs, targeting about 10,923 values per CTA with 256 threads, may retain more input parallelism than the previously slow 256-CTA configuration while reducing output-atomic contention relative to the measured 512-CTA candidate. This tests an unmeasured point; the prior 512-CTA/8192-target result averaged 6.341 µs, while the 256-CTA/16384-target result averaged 14.860 µs, and their multiple parameter differences do not establish a cause.

transformations: Add a one-thread output-zeroing kernel followed by a 256-thread grid-stride kernel for n >= 1<<20, both launched in default-stream order.
Use a 384-CTA cap and a target of 10,923 input values per CTA; each CTA performs unsigned 32-bit accumulation, warp/shared-memory reduction, and one unsigned int32 atomicAdd to out.
For n <= 0, enqueue an output-zero kernel; retain the original hierarchical reduction and output copy for positive n below the threshold.
